newsitem.title: USA: Chinese restaurant owner testifies against McVeigh.
newsitem.headline: Chinese restaurant owner testifies against McVeigh.

text.p: The owner of a Chinese restaurant testified Friday that she took a food order over the phone from a "Mr Kling," the pseudonym prosecutors claim Timothy McVeigh used to rent the Ryder truck that blew up the Oklahoma City federal building.

In damaging testimony, the owner said she sent a delivery man to the motel room where McVeigh had registered under his own name in Junction City, Kansas, on April 14, 1995, five days before the explosion.
The prosecution contends that McVeigh rented the truck in Junction City and drove it full of explosives to Oklahoma City about five hours away.
McVeigh has denied he planned and carried out the blast, which killed 168 people.
Also appearing as a witness for the prosecution was Marife Nichols, the Philippine-born wife of McVeigh's alleged co- conspirator Terry Nichols, who will be tried separately later.

Prosecutors have presented more than 80 witnesses in the past two weeks who have either testitifed about McVeigh's anger at the governmment, his efforts to buy components to make the bomb, or the pre-paid telephone card that he allegedly used when planning the bombing.

Yuhua Bai, the owner of the Hunan Palace, testified that the caller placed an order for egg rolls and another dish on April 15, and said she noticed the name "Kling" because it sounded like a Chinese name.

Marife Nichols testified that while the family was eating dinner on Easter Sunday -- three days before the bombing -- her husband received a telephone call. She said he left the house 15 minutes later and she did not see him until the next morning.
McVeigh did not look at her while she spoke. Outside the court, her lawyer told reporters that she stood by her husband even though she testified in a limited manner for the prosecution.
